description: Behavioural evals for the design-sensei skill, in skill-creator's evals.json format. Authored but not yet run. Each eval is a realistic task prompt plus verifiable expectations; grade them against the transcript and outputs of a with-skill run, and compare with a baseline run of the same prompt without the skill. Input file paths are relative to the repository root.

evals.name: greenfield-handmade-landing-page
evals.prompt: I run a tiny ceramics studio in Bristol called Tidepool Clay and we sell Saturday wheel-throwing workshops (12 people max, 85 GBP). I need a one-page site, plain HTML/CSS/JS, saved to ./out/index.html. No brand yet, no logo. I really don't want it to look like a SaaS landing page, it should feel handmade. Most of our visitors are on phones.
evals.expected_output: A single-page site in ./out/ that follows a written art-direction brief, uses a deliberate style from the catalog rather than a default template look, is usable at 375 px, and reports honestly how it was checked.
expectations: Writes an art-direction brief (audience and emotion, style, typography, colour, layout, motion) with a one-line reason per decision before it writes any HTML or CSS
Runs `design-sensei search` or `design-sensei recommend` (or reads the pattern index or catalog directly if the command is unavailable) to pick a style or pattern instead of choosing from memory
Names one primary style direction and does not combine more than one supporting influence
Avoids the generic tells: no default indigo-to-violet gradient, no centred hero over three identical icon cards, no single typeface used for everything
Provides a prefers-reduced-motion path for any animation it adds
Says explicitly what it could not verify (for example real devices, screen readers, other browsers) or shows evidence of what it did check (for example screenshots at 375 px)
Does not add a dependency or build step that the request did not need

evals.name: scroll-storytelling-with-licence-question
evals.prompt: In my Vite + React + TypeScript app (src/components/ProductStory.tsx, gsap is already in package.json) I want a pinned scroll-driven story: 4 steps, the phone mockup rotates and the copy swaps as you scroll. Use the best open-source implementation you can find rather than inventing something, but this is for a paying client so I need to know whether I'm actually allowed to reuse it.
evals.expected_output: A scroll-driven component adapted from a traced catalog pattern, with the pattern's source id and licence class stated, plus a reduced-motion alternative.
expectations: Searches the pattern catalog (for example `design-sensei search scroll ...`) and reads the matching pattern or recipe before implementing
Names the catalog pattern id and the upstream source id for every borrowed idea
States the licence class (reuse class) of each borrowed pattern, such as copy_with_attribution, license_review_required or reimplement_only, in plain words
Does not copy code from a source whose reuse class forbids copying (reference_only, reimplement_only, verify_first); it re-implements the idea instead
Keeps one animation system by using the GSAP already installed rather than adding Motion or a second scroll library without justification
Gives a prefers-reduced-motion alternative that still shows all four steps of content
Lists any new dependency in its summary, or says that none were added

evals.name: shader-hero-with-fallbacks
evals.prompt: Take examples/glass-hero/index.html and put a slow, subtle animated shader gradient behind the glass panel instead of the CSS blobs. I want it to feel like moving ink in water. It has to run fine on a mid-range Android phone and the page must still look good if WebGL is unavailable.
evals.expected_output: A WebGL fragment-shader background wired into the existing page, with a static fallback, reduced-motion handling and cleanup, built within the existing CSS token system.
expectations: Inspects the existing index.html and styles.css and extends them instead of rewriting the page from scratch
Provides a static fallback (CSS gradient or the existing blobs) that is used when WebGL is unavailable or the context is lost
Honours prefers-reduced-motion by not animating, or by rendering a single still frame
Limits GPU cost for mobile (for example capped device pixel ratio, low-resolution render target, or a small number of noise octaves) and says what it chose
Pauses rendering when the canvas is offscreen or the tab is hidden, and cleans up its animation frame and GPU resources
Marks the canvas as decorative (aria-hidden) and keeps text contrast over the shader acceptable
States which checks it ran (for example `design-sensei eval`, a screenshot) and which it could not run

evals.name: r3f-viewer-without-browser-tool
evals.prompt: Add a 3D product viewer to my Next.js 14 app router project for our wireless headphones. The model is at public/models/cans.glb, react-three-fiber and drei are already installed. Orbit with inertia, soft studio lighting, and a gentle idle rotation. Heads up: this machine has no browser and no GPU, so you can only run the build and lint.
evals.expected_output: A client-only R3F viewer component with sensible performance and fallback behaviour, and a summary that is candid about what could not be verified without a browser.
expectations: States plainly in the final summary that the viewer was not visually inspected and lists what could not be verified (rendering, frame rate, touch behaviour, WebGL fallback)
Does not claim the result looks good or performs well without evidence
Loads the 3D code client-side only and lazily (for example dynamic import with ssr disabled or Suspense), so it does not bloat the initial bundle
Provides a static poster image or fallback when WebGL is unavailable, and a reduced-motion setting that disables the idle rotation
Reuses the installed react-three-fiber and drei rather than adding a competing 3D library
Runs the project's own build or lint as the only checks that were available and reports their result
Writes a short art-direction note (lighting mood, background, motion tempo) before the code

evals.name: restrained-polish-no-new-effects
evals.prompt: Our docs site header (site/Header.astro) looks a bit dated next to the rest of the page. Please modernise it, but keep it quiet: it's developer documentation, people are here to read. No WebGL, no animation libraries, no new dependencies, and please keep our existing CSS variables.
evals.expected_output: A restrained refresh of the header that respects the stated constraints and shows judgement about how much design ambition the context calls for.
expectations: Inspects the existing header and CSS variables before changing anything and states which tokens it will reuse
Adds no WebGL, canvas, 3D or animation library and no new dependency
Sets a low motion and low experimental ambition in its art-direction note, with a reason tied to the documentation audience
Keeps the change small and readable: the diff touches the header and its styles, not the whole site
Preserves or improves accessibility: visible focus styles, sufficient contrast, keyboard-operable navigation
Does not use glass, glow or gradient effects as decoration unless it justifies them for this audience
